title: Seaming and Assembly Basics
description: Join crochet pieces neatly so the finished project feels sturdy, smooth, and intentional.

content.summary: Seaming connects separate panels or motifs with a method that matches the stretch and finish you want.
content.whyItMatters: Clean assembly makes simple projects look polished, improves fit, and helps pieces hold their shape over time.
steps: Lay the pieces in the correct orientation before joining anything.
Match corners, row ends, or stitch counts with markers so both sides line up.
Choose a joining method such as whip stitch, mattress-style seaming, slip stitch, or single crochet edging.
Join with even tension so the seam feels secure without becoming stiff.
Check the right side often to make sure the seam stays straight and tidy.
content.practice: Join two small swatches with two different methods so you can compare stretch, thickness, and appearance.
commonMistakes: Pulling the seam tighter than the fabric itself.
